youtube.title: Why Bread Goes Stale (It's Not Drying Out) 🍞 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
Bread goes stale mainly because of starch retrogradation, not because it dries out. Baking gelatinises the starch, which soaks up water and softens. As the loaf cools, the starch molecules slowly realign into stiff crystals and push water out, so the crumb firms up. Fridge temperatures speed this up, which is why refrigerated bread stales faster, and reheating or toasting reverses it for a while.

sources: Gray & BeMiller, Bread staling: molecular basis and control (Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science, 2003)
Staling is fastest near refrigerator temperatures and partly reversed by reheating above ~60 C
